action: Receive the request (form or email to the DPO), check the person's identity and log it in the request register
Find every source record of the person through the golden-customer mapping table (emails and phones of all their records)
Add a hash of the person's emails and phones to the erasure suppression list: staging models filter these people out at every sync, so data re-sent by a source tool never comes back
Delete the person in Klaviyo and Zendesk, and request erasure in Shopify (Shopify completes it after 10 days, or up to 6 months after the last order; orders stay, anonymized)
Delete the person's rows in the raw layer by their source ids
Run VACUUM on the affected Delta tables so old file versions holding the data are removed (Delta keeps old versions 7 days by default)
Delete the person's row in the golden-customer mapping table and rebuild the customer staging models with dbt
Rebuild dim_customer; fact rows of the person keep only the anonymous customer key (-1), so sales totals stay correct
Refresh the Power BI semantic models; check that no exported file or report page shows the person (exports contain customer keys only)
Platform backups expire after 30 days; the register notes the date when the last backup holding the data disappears
Confirm to the person that the erasure is done (Shopify's delay is explained if it applies) and close the request in the register
Remove the person from the suppression list once Shopify has completed its erasure
